skill1: ■ Activates when using Burst Skill. Affects self if not in Nano Coating status. — Nano Coating: Creates a Shield equal to 21.12% of the skill user's final Max HP continuously. (UNREACHABLE at scope lock: the battle-start Shield from the first header carries no duration and the v1 boss deals no damage, so the owner is in Nano Coating status from frame 0 for the whole fight and the 'if not in Nano Coating' branch can never fire. The engine also has no 'not shielded' block gate — requiresShielded is a boolean whose only documented semantic is 'shielded'.)
skill2: ■ Activates when using Burst Skill while not in Nano Coating status. Affects self. Effects vary according to the number of uses. Each subsequent effect triggers all effects before it: — Once: Next Shield's HP ▲ 17.75% continuously. / Twice: Next Shield's HP ▲ 26.66% continuously. / Three times: Next Shield's HP ▲ 35.53% continuously. (Triple-unmodelable: (a) the 'while not in Nano Coating status' gate is unreachable at scope lock and inexpressible in the schema; (b) there is no StatKey for Shield HP magnitude; (c) no shield HP pool is modeled at all — the 'shield' effect records maxHpPct for kit completeness and emits the event only.)
burst: ■ Activates when not in Nano Coating status. Affects self. — Max HP ▲ 48% for 20 sec. (UNREACHABLE at scope lock, same reason as the skill1 branch. Encoded as targetMaxHpPct it would fire on EVERY burst and over-credit; the owner carries no atkOfMaxHpPct so it is offensively inert today, but it WOULD raise the HP basis of the Nano-Coating burst nuke if that nuke is ever given a true Max-HP basis — the two branches are mutually exclusive in the kit, so the interaction is moot in-game.)

caveats: ⚑ HP-BASIS DAMAGE — the burst's atkPct 575 is a PLACEHOLDER, not the kit number. The kit deals 1150.84% of an ATK computed from 5% of final Max HP; the schema's flatDamage.atkPct scales off final ATK only, so the value shown is a converted estimate and is WRONG by the ratio of this unit's real Max HP to her ATK. This is the single largest source of error in the file.
⚑ Every ⚑ magnitude here is derived from kit text plus modeling convention — nothing in this file has been measured against a real fight.

⚑ The burst nuke's crit:true follows the rider-crit convention; noFb is deliberately unset (default ON by timing). Burst-cast damage is understood to land before the Full Burst window opens, so the +50% major should not apply — but that is engine-level behaviour, not asserted here.
⚑ The skill2 shield-restore cadence (hitCount 200) depends on the MG's real fire cadence and reload, both from datamine-unreliable fields; its real per-fight fire count is unverified.

SCOPE-LOCK DETERMINISM: three of the seven kit lines are gated on 'not in Nano Coating status'. Because the skill1 shield is continuous and the v1 boss deals no damage, the owner is permanently coated, so those three lines are dead at scope lock and are recorded in `unmodeled` rather than modeled behind an unexpressible negative gate. If shield-breaking is ever modeled, this file needs a real duty-cycle (a `modes` toggle or a negative shield gate).
override.note: PARSER BASELINE (HYPOTHESIS — NOT a validated model). Every ⚑ below is an UNMEASURED estimate; hand-tune + record against a real fight before trusting any number. Kilo (MG/Fire/Defender/B3) is a shield-state kit whose every branch reads one self-status, Nano Coating. S1 grants a continuous Shield of 21.12% of her own final Max HP at battle start; at scope lock the boss deals no damage and the shield carries no duration, so she is coated from frame 0 to the end of the fight. That single fact collapses the kit: the coated branches always fire and the uncoated branches never do. Modeled: the battle-start shield (passive/self), the S2 shield restore after 200 rounds while coated (hitCount 200 + requiresShielded), and the burst nuke (burstCast + requiresShielded, target enemy). The burst nuke's magnitude is the file's weak point — the kit's 1150.84% is applied to an ATK derived from 5% of her final Max HP, and the schema has no HP-basis damage effect, so atkPct 575 is a converted placeholder (see caveats). Deliberately unmodeled: the three 'while not in Nano Coating' lines (the burst-cast shield re-grant, the escalating Next-Shield-HP buffs, and the Max HP ▲48% burst branch) — all unreachable at scope lock, and the escalating buffs additionally have no schema stat and no shield HP pool behind them. Her shield effects target self only, so they drive her own `shielded` triggers and nothing on a teammate; they are offensively inert today but are kept because shield/heal lines are never skipped on isolation.

flags.reasoning: The kit states 1150.84% of an ATK that is itself 5% of final Max HP, i.e. true damage = 1150.84% x 0.05 x finalMaxHp = 57.5% of final Max HP. The schema has no HP-basis damage effect (flatDamage.atkPct is % of final ATK), so an ATK-equivalent conversion is required: atkPct = 1150.84 x 0.05 x (finalMaxHp / finalAtk). The ratio is NOT in the kit text and no Max HP figure was supplied in the base stats, so it cannot be derived from the input domain. Assuming a scope-lock Defender Max-HP-to-ATK ratio in the ~9-11x band gives 5% of Max HP at roughly 0.45-0.55 x ATK, hence ~518-633% of ATK; 575 is the midpoint. This is a first estimate, NOT a kit number, and it is the dominant error term in this file.
flags.recipe: Two routes. (1) CHEAP/CORRECT-BY-CONSTRUCTION: add an `hpPct` basis field to `flatDamage` (precedent already exists on `stackedNuke.hpPct`, '% of final Max HP added on top') and author the line as its literal 57.5% of final Max HP, removing the estimate entirely. (2) STOPGAP: read this unit's finalMaxHp and finalAtk at the scope-lock preset from data/characters.json plus the gear/sync stack, compute atkPct = 57.542 x (finalMaxHp / finalAtk), and pin it in a scripts/tests/units/kilo.test.ts assertion so a later stat change cannot silently invalidate it. Route (1) is strongly preferred: route (2) hard-codes a stat ratio into a damage number and breaks the moment sync/gear/any Max HP buff moves.

flags.field: burst[0] / skill1[1] / skill2[1] — the 'not in Nano Coating' negative gate
flags.estimate: Gate is permanently FALSE at scope lock; the three uncoated branches are dead
flags.reasoning: The schema's `requiresShielded` is documented only for the positive case ('the block only activates while the OWNER currently has a shield set on them'), and its own doc note states that a shield with no duration is permanent at scope because boss damage is unmodeled and nothing breaks shields. Since S1 grants exactly such a shield at frame 0, the owner is coated for the entire fight and every 'while not in Nano Coating' line is unreachable. Encoding those lines WITHOUT the gate would over-credit them on every burst; encoding them WITH a `requiresShielded:false` would rely on a semantic the engine does not implement (falsy reads as unconstrained). They are therefore recorded verbatim in `unmodeled` rather than modeled.
flags.recipe: If shield-breaking is ever modeled (a boss that deals damage, or an explicit shield HP pool), the kit needs a real duty cycle. Two encodings: (a) a negative shield gate, e.g. widening requiresShielded to 'shielded' | 'unshielded' mirroring fbGate/swapGate/ownBurstGate, which is the shape the rest of the schema already uses for two-sided state gates; or (b) a top-level `modes: ['nanoCoated','uncoated']` toggle with `mode` gates per block, which is user-selectable but does not track the state dynamically. (a) is the faithful one. Until then, confirm from footage that the shield genuinely never drops in a real solo-raid fight — if it does, this file's burst branch is wrong on those rotations.

flags.estimate: Fires roughly once per ~1.5 magazines; real per-fight count unknown
flags.reasoning: The threshold (200 rounds) is literal kit text and is NOT flagged. What is flagged is how often 200 rounds actually accrue: that depends on the MG's pulls-per-second and reloadFrames, both from datamine fields the modeling priors mark unreliable, plus MG wind-up. With a 300-round belt the trigger lands partway through each magazine, so its per-fight count is sensitive to cadence error. The effect is offensively inert today, so this flag is about future correctness (a shield-synergy consumer keyed to her `shielded` events would inherit the error), not about current damage.
flags.recipe: Score the modeled shot count against a real recording: count her rounds fired over a fixed window from footage (ammo counter is the direct instrument for shots/sec, not full-burst counts, which are downstream of gauge), and compare against the sim's shot events. If a labeled cadence fixture for this weapon class already exists in scripts/tests/** or docs/probe-data/, run against it instead — that IS the independent method and no new recording is needed.

flags.estimate: unset (Full Burst by timing, default ON)
flags.reasoning: Per the ALWAYS-⚑ taxonomy, per-kit noFb is default OFF and measured-only, so it is deliberately not set here. Separately, the standing convention is that burst-cast damage lands before the Full Burst window opens and therefore takes no +50% major and no entry auras — but that is engine-level timing behaviour for burstCast-triggered damage, not something this override should assert per-unit. If the engine does NOT already exempt burst-cast damage, this nuke is over-credited by 1.5x.
flags.recipe: Read the burstCast damage path in the engine and confirm the pre-FB snapshot behaviour; if it is already handled, leave noFb unset permanently and note it. If it is not, the fix belongs in the engine (it affects every burst-slot nuke on the roster), not in this file — do not paper over it with a per-unit noFb.

flags.reasoning: Convention: function-damage riders crit at the caster's sheet rate, and get NO core unless the kit text literally says 'core strike damage' (it does not here, so core is omitted). Setting crit follows the rider-crit rule rather than a measurement of this specific unit.
flags.recipe: Confirm from a focus recording of her burst: an orange popup with the crit icon on the nuke confirms crit-eligible; a consistently white popup at the same magnitude across many casts refutes it. A single cast is not sufficient — the crit rate at scope lock is well below 100%, so absence in one sample proves nothing.

flags.reasoning: The `shield` effect models no HP pool in v1 (the boss deals no damage), so maxHpPct is stored for kit completeness and to emit the `shielded` event; the numbers themselves change nothing today. They are kit-literal, so this is a visibility flag, not an estimate. The event emission IS load-bearing for the requiresShielded gates in this same file, and would become load-bearing for any teammate with a shield-synergy trigger.
flags.recipe: No measurement needed while shields are unmodeled. If a shield HP pool is ever added, these two values plus the skipped 'Next Shield's HP ▲' escalation become live and must be re-authored together — the escalation multiplies the NEXT shield, so ordering against the 200-round restore matters.
